notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.46_x64-setup.exe`.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.46.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.46.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.

---

A bug-fix release. Ruze now has a test suite that runs real devices against
each other, and everything below is something it found.

### Changed

- **A direct message's notification says who it is from and what they
  said.** It used to read "Ada replied to you" over "#Direct message — hi",
  as though it were a reply in a channel that does not exist.

### Fixed

- **Nobody loses a server when it changes hands.** Handing a server to
  somebody else stopped it working for everybody in it, and on a private
  server everyone the old owner had let in lost their place. Starting a new
  account did the same to the servers you owned. Ownership now moves as a
  signed record kept in the server, and everything the previous owner set up
  goes on working.

- **Demoting an admin no longer takes their channels with them.** A channel
  an admin made became unreadable to everybody, the owner included, the day
  they were demoted. The people an admin let in keep their access too.

- **What an admin does is seen by everybody.** An admin could rename a server
  and make channels, and nobody else ever saw either.

- **Editing a message in a private channel no longer makes it disappear.**
  The edit vanished for everyone, you included, and its text was written
  unencrypted. Every new text channel is private, so this was every edit.

- **Calls:** a join that never got an answer left every join button stuck on
  "Connecting…" until you restarted; people who had left could stay in the
  room on somebody's screen; the camera could turn on for a call you had
  already left; and a dragged volume slider could jump back. When a room's
  host leaves, whoever is left can rename it.

- **Private channels can't be undermined by a member.** A member could make
  a channel be written in plain text, plant a key that locked others out, or
  hide the server's name and channels from everybody. None of that works now.

- **Nobody can delete your messages but you.** Another member could take your
  messages off everybody's screen, and in one case delete them for good.

- **Friends:** every pair of friends kept rewriting each other's cards for as
  long as both apps were open; two friend requests arriving at once
  befriended nobody; and renaming a server or making it private didn't reach
  your friends.

- **Refusals arrive.** Declining a friend request, a join or a device pairing
  looked like "they stopped answering" at the other end, which then asked
  again.

- **Messages:** an edit was counted as a new unread message and chimed again;
  a message arriving while its conversation was loading could vanish until it
  was reopened; new messages threw away history you had scrolled back into; a
  channel's messages were counted as read while you were looking at your
  friends; reactions could go missing when you switched channels quickly; and
  one pasted screenshot was attached twice.

- **Smaller things:** a server name starting with an emoji put half of it on
  the badge; a server's icon could go stale or show the wrong picture;
  tooltips could jump to the wrong button; shortcuts recorded Control as
  Command on a Mac and the Windows key as Ctrl; a window against the left edge
  of the screen didn't reopen there on Windows; and an emoji that failed to
  load once while you were offline never animated again that session.
